name: Walker's Dictionary
author: John Walker
description: Sample entries from 'A Critical Pronouncing Dictionary and Expositor of the English Language' (1791). Walker's dictionary was influential for its focus on pronunciation and refined definitions.

entries.definition: The author of a dictionary; one whose employment is to write dictionaries.
A grain of great use for the food of horses, and of the common people in the northern parts of Britain.
One who protects, supports, or countenances; a guardian saint; an advocate; a defender.
A stated allowance to any person in consideration of past services.
A tax levied upon commodities.
Heat of imagination; violence of passion; elevation of fancy; exaltation of ideas.
The power of combining heterogeneous ideas with quickness and propriety; a man of genius; a man of fancy.
Any thing made with interstices or decussations.
A fictitious narrative in prose; a tale of adventures and love.
A member of one of the two great political parties in Britain.
A member of one of the two great political parties in Britain, opposed to the Tory.
A trial; an endeavour; a loose sally of the mind; an irregular piece.
A heavy stick; an assembly of companions meeting for some common purpose.
The power of forming ideal pictures; the power of representing absent things to ourselves and others; an idea; a fancy.
The power of invention; the peculiar character or disposition of men or nations; a man endowed with superior faculties.
Celebrity; renown; report; public estimation.
An expectation of good with some degree of probability.
An apprehension of danger or pain; dread; anxiety; awe.
The passion between the sexes; tenderness; affection; kindness; good-will.
Moral goodness; efficacy; excellence; bravery.
The system of the world; the regular course of things; disposition; constitution.
The power of doing what is not taught by nature; a science; skill; trade; artifice.
Knowledge; certainty grounded on demonstration; any branch of speculative knowledge.
Knowledge natural or moral; the study of natural or moral causes; reasoning; argumentation.
Freedom opposed to slavery; freedom opposed to necessity; privilege; permission.
The virtue by which we give every one their due; equity; vindictive retribution.
A book in which the words of a language are explained in alphabetical order.
The science of speaking or writing a language with propriety.
The descent or derivation of a word from its original.
Human speech; the speech of one nation as distinguished from others; style; expression.
